newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand seen signalling rate cut Monday.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand seen signalling rate cut Monday.

text.p: Thai Bankers Association President Olarn Chaiprawat said he expects the Bank of Thailand on Monday to signal an interest rate cut was ahead.
"The Bank of Thailand is expected to make an unequivocal statement on the direction of interest rates, which will go downward," Olarn told reporters on Sunday, but declined to elaborate.
Bank of Thailand deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Friday the central bank would call a press conference at 11.00 am (0400 GMT) on Monday to announce new monetary measures.
He did not elaborate on what measures were planned.
Olarn who is also the president of Siam Commercial Bank Plc said the central bank is also expected to come up with new measures to formally separate the offshore and onshore foreign exchange markets.
He downplayed concern that such a system could affect capital inflows needed to finance Thailand's current account deficit.
Olarn said Thailand could subscribe to the same forex system as Singapore.
"We encourage non-volatile long-term capital inflow," Olarn said.
Olarn said a stable forex market would provide more flexibility in Thailand's interest rate policy in future.
He added that commercial banks were likely to cut their lending rates a few days after the central bank made its statement on Monday.
"But it won't go down as much as 50 basis points in one cut as speculated," Olarn said.
Olarn said he wants to see the lending rates come down by 100 to 200 basis points this year.

Thailand's minimum lending rate stands at around 12.75-13.00 percent, among the highest in the region. The central bank keeps rates high to encourage capital inflows and to defend the baht against speculative attacks.
"This rate cut will not revive the economy, but at least it can hold the economy," he said.
"It also depends on a lot of other factors. If you asked me whether I want to see the rates come down. I would say I fight for it everyday. But I'm only one of the horses in the race."
